packages.label: כָּבוֹד עֶלְיוֹן וּמַאֲמָר סָתוּם
packages.label_en: Supreme Hidden Glory and the Sealed Utterance
packages.reason: These concepts all share the same essential nature: the utterly concealed, transcendent dimension of God's glory that is the root of all creation, yet cannot be grasped by intellect. The Rebbe explicitly states: 'אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ – זֶה בְּחִינַת הַכָּבוֹד עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁל הַמַּאֲמָר הָעֶלְיוֹן, דְּהַיְנוּ הַמַּאֲמָר סָתוּם בְּרֵאשִׁית' (line 12) and 'כִּי אַיֵּה הוּא בְּחִינוֹת מַאֲמָר סָתוּם' (line 23). These three — 'אַיֵּה', 'כָּבוֹד עֶלְיוֹן', 'מַאֲמָר סָתוּם בְּרֵאשִׁית' — are explicitly identified as the same bechina from multiple directions. Additionally, שֶׂה לְעֹלָה (the Akeidah sacrifice) is called 'בְּחִינוֹת שֶׂה לְעוֹלָה' that equals 'בְּחִינַת אַיֵּה' (line 16), and the חָלָל הַפָּנוּי (the apparently void space) is also identified as sustained by this same maamar satum (line 27). The binding principle across all nodes is: the absolute hiddenness that transcends the revealed utterances — their shared nature is transcendent concealment as the root of life.

merge_notes.reason: Core triangle: all three are explicitly identified as the same bechina by the Rebbe in lines 12 and 23. 'אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ' = the upper kavod = the maamar satum. This is the densest bechina cluster in the Torah.

Line 16: 'שֶׁבְּחִינַת אַיֵּה הִיא בְּחִינוֹת שֶׂה לְעוֹלָה'. The Akeidah sacrifice IS the same bechina as 'אַיֵּה', which is the same bechina as the supreme kavod. Shared nature: the ascent-through-concealment that redeems.

Line 27: the chalal hapanui (apparently vacant space, seemingly devoid of divinity) receives life specifically from the maamar satum. The chalal's essential nature IS that it is sustained by the same hidden source. Both are expressions of the same hiddenness-that-gives-life.

packages.label: כָּבוֹד גָּלוּי וַעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת
packages.label_en: Revealed Glory and the Ten Utterances
packages.reason: These concepts share the essential nature of the revealed, bounded dimension of divine glory — the glory that is manifest in the world through the ten utterances of creation. The Rebbe states (line 5): 'בְּכָל מַאֲמָר וּמַאֲמָר יֵשׁ בּוֹ בְּחִינַת כָּבוֹד מְיֻחָד' — each utterance contains a particular bechina of kavod as its root. The verse 'וּבְהֵיכָלוֹ כֻּלּוֹ אֹמֵר כָּבוֹד' (Psalms 29:9) is called the bechina of this structure (line 6): 'שֶׁבְּכָל מַאֲמָר מְלֻבָּשׁ בּוֹ כְּבוֹדוֹ'. The שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה (root of all creation) is explicitly identified as כָּבוֹד in line 4. These nodes share the nature of bounded/revealed divine glory — kavod as it flows into and sustains the structure of the world.

merge_notes.reason: Line 4: 'כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא הַכָּבוֹד' — kavod IS the root of all creation. These are two names for the same essential reality. Shared nature: the cosmic ground of all existence.

Lines 5-6: each of the ten utterances contains a specific bechina of kavod as its root. The ten utterances are the revealed structure through which kavod is expressed in the world. Shared nature: revealed divine glory subdivided into the world's structure.

Line 2: the entire teaching opens with the prescription of temimut/peshitut as the antidote to relying on one's own sekhel, and this is immediately connected to acting only for 'כְּבוֹד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ'. The walk of simplicity and the orientation toward God's kavod are two expressions of the same essential alignment — temimut IS the direct connection to kavod. One who goes in peshitut automatically acts for kevod Hashem rather than his own kavod. Shared nature: the correct human orientation toward divine glory.

packages.label: קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ וּסְפֵקוֹת
packages.reason: These concepts share the essential nature of the obstructing/confusing force that twists the heart and generates doubt — the domain of the kelipah that sits at the boundary between holiness and impurity. The Rebbe makes two explicit bechina statements: (1) line 14: 'לִבִּי סְחַרְחַר ... וְהִיא בְּחִינַת קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ ... וְנֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב' — the circular/twisting heart IS klipat nogah; (2) line 19: 'וְאֵלּוּ הַסְּפֵקוֹת הֵם בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת נֹגַהּ' — the doubts and confusions ARE eitz hada'at tov vera, which IS nogah. Thus: סְפֵקוֹת = עֵץ הַדַּעַת = קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ = לִבִּי סְחַרְחַר. All are faces of the same mixed/churning reality at the boundary of holiness. The מְקוֹמוֹת הַמְטֻנָּפִים (polluted places, places of sin and confusion) are explicitly identified as the domain where one falls when dominated by this force.

merge_notes.reason: Line 14: explicitly stated as bechina. 'לִבִּי סְחַרְחַר' (my heart goes around/twists) = klipat nogah = 'וְנֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב' (Ezekiel 1:4). The circular spinning of the confused heart IS the essential nature of klipat nogah.

Line 19: 'אֵלּוּ הַסְּפֵקוֹת הֵם בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת נֹגַהּ'. Double bechina chain: doubts = eitz hada'at = nogah. All three are the same force of mixture and confusion.

Lines 11 and 15: falling to 'מְקוֹמוֹת הַמְטֻנָּפִים' is synonymous with falling into doubts and confusions. The polluted places are the existential location of klipat nogah's domain — they are two expressions of the same fallen state. Shared nature: the domain of mixed/polluted spiritual reality.

packages.label: תְּשׁוּבָה וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים
packages.label_en: Return and the Tree of Life
packages.reason: These concepts share the essential nature of the soul's return/ascent from the fallen state — the process of reconnection with divine glory. The Rebbe calls the act of seeking 'אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ' by the name teshuvah (line 18): 'וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה'. He also calls it the bechina of the olah sacrifice (line 13): 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת קָרְבָּן עוֹלָה, שֶׁמְּכַפֵּר עַל הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב'. And he states that arriving at the Torah itself (after passing through the doubts) is the bechina of eitz hachayyim (line 19): 'וּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ אֶל הַתּוֹרָה בְּעַצְמָהּ, זֶה בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַחַיִּים'. The shared nature across all these nodes is: the active return-to-holiness through seeking God's glory — the rectification process that is the polar opposite of the doubts/kelipah cluster.

merge_notes.reason: Lines 13 and 18: the olah sacrifice atones for hirhurim (contemplations), which is the same as teshuvah — both are the rectification of the heart's fall into doubts. Shared nature: the mechanism of ascent/atonement from the fallen state.

Line 19: arriving at the Torah itself (after passing through the doubts) = bechina of eitz hachayyim. This arrival IS the teshuvah — returning through the Torah to the Tree of Life is the completion of the ascent. Shared nature: the destination of the return — pure Torah/holiness without mixture.

Lines 3 and 11: the descent is explicitly called 'תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה' (the ultimate ascent). The fall into doubts that results in seeking God's glory IS the teshuvah. 'יְרִידָה תַּכְלִית הָעֲלִיָּה' and תְּשׁוּבָה share the same essential structure: the inverted dynamic where the fall generates the highest rise. Shared nature: the paradoxical ascent-through-descent that characterizes genuine return.

good_evil_mirror.package_2_good: כָּבוֹד גָּלוּי — the revealed glory that structures the world through the ten utterances
good_evil_mirror.package_3_evil: קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ — the mixed/churning force that distorts and confuses, blocking access to kavod
good_evil_mirror.mirror_analysis: The evil package (3) is the exact mirror of the good package (2): where kavod fills and structures creation, kelipat nogah twists and confuses. The ten utterances contain bounded kavod; klipat nogah is the distorted reception of that boundary. The doubts (sfeikot) arise precisely because one is at the boundary between the utterances' specific kavod and the outer spaces. Package 1 (hidden glory) resolves the mirror by transcending both — the maamar satum is above the good/evil boundary of the revealed utterances.
